solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Toast last drink (7,2)

blocks.note: a cheery phrase said as glasses are raised
the call to drain the glass, tipping its base skywards

annotation.surface: Someone raises a glass for one final round before closing time.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves are about drinking, so the clue reads as one idea; the second half pictures the glass tipped until its base points at the ceiling.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase is spoken as a drinking salute, and literally describes emptying glasses by tipping their bases upward.

entries.clue: Loose goods stored in compartment (5)

indicatorNotes.stored in: goods that are stored are put away inside something, here the compartment

blocks.note: a bay is a compartment, as in a loading bay or bomb bay

annotation.surface: Some loose goods have been stowed in a compartment of a van or ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loose goods' reads as one phrase, but 'Loose' is the definition, split off from the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Clothes that hang off the body without fitting snugly are described as baggy.

entries.clue: Treating Sheffield chums to a classic performance at The Crucible? (3,7,2,5)

indicatorNotes.Treating: to treat something is to process it, as with chemicals, changing it into a new form

annotation.surface: A Sheffield local takes friends out for an evening of classic theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The Crucible is Sheffield's main theatre, best known abroad for snooker, so the fodder's Sheffield fits the scene. 'Treating ... to' reads as buying tickets; 'to a' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Webster's Jacobean tragedy is a classic that the Sheffield Crucible could well stage; the question mark marks it as an example.

entries.clue: Maybe sweaty husband enters having too much on his plate? (11)

indicatorNotes.enters: the husband walks in among the letters of the overeating word

blocks.clueFragment: having too much on his plate

annotation.surface: A man at a dinner is sweating over a heaped plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too much on his plate' usually means being overworked; here it is taken literally as food.
annotation.definitionFit: A body running too hot sweats, so sweaty is one possible sign of it, which is why 'Maybe' is there.

entries.clue: In America, civilians perhaps turning up to register for the dole (4,2)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning something up flips it so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers, so civilians are NON-GIs

annotation.surface: Out-of-work Americans head in to claim unemployment benefit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The dole' is British for unemployment benefit.
annotation.definitionFit: British jobseekers claim unemployment benefit by adding their names at the benefit office each fortnight.

entries.clue: Complain about neckwear Charlie’s wearing in rehearsal (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned round, as in 'about turn', so the word is reversed
indicatorNotes.wearing: the tie wears Charlie on it, so the letter sits inside the tie

blocks.note: a tie is worn round the neck
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An actor grumbles about the tie a colleague called Charlie wears at rehearsals.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a person wearing neckwear; it is only a letter, and the tie is what wears it.
annotation.definitionFit: A run-through before the real performance is both a rehearsal and a session of preparation for it.

entries.clue: “The Greatest” wingers from Goodison stand in a row (5)

indicatorNotes.wingers from: wingers play out on the edges of the pitch, so take the two edge letters

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

annotation.surface: The club's star wide men line up at Goodison, Everton's ground.
annotation.walkthrough: Goodison Park is the home of Everton football club, so 'wingers' reads as players; it means the word's edges.
annotation.definitionFit: Objects brought into a straight line, each level with the next, are placed in a row.

entries.clue: Vulnerable area which mother didn’t bathe? (8,4)

annotation.definition: Vulnerable area which mother didn’t bathe?

blocks.note: sounds like a sore spot on a baby's skin, or a weak point in general
in Greek myth the sea-nymph Thetis dipped her son in the Styx, holding him by one foot

annotation.surface: A parent missed a patch when bathing a child.
annotation.walkthrough: Thetis dipped her baby in the River Styx to make him invulnerable, but the spot she held stayed dry, and an arrow there killed him at Troy.
annotation.definitionFit: The Greek hero's one unprotected spot gave the phrase for any single weakness in otherwise strong defences.

entries.clue: Legal disqualification of secretary in Machu Picchu? (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the secretary is placed in, inside the city's description

blocks.note: Machu Picchu is an Inca city in Peru

annotation.surface: A secretary stationed at Machu Picchu is found unfit for legal purposes.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Machu Picchu stands for a description of itself, not a place.
annotation.definitionFit: In law, lacking the legal power to act, as a minor cannot sign contracts, is termed incapacity.

entries.clue: Arrest former pupil, a rich and powerful man (5)

annotation.surface: Police arrest an old boy of a school who turns out to be a tycoon.
annotation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
annotation.definitionFit: The word first named Europeans who made fortunes in India, and now any wealthy grandee.

entries.clue: Stay twenty four hours in Paris, very new surroundings (7)

indicatorNotes.surroundings: the very-new letters form the surroundings that enclose the Paris day

annotation.surface: A day's stay in Paris in quite unfamiliar surroundings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very new surroundings' reads as strange places; it is two words split around the French day.
annotation.definitionFit: A temporary stay somewhere away from home is a sojourn, a word from Old French for spending the day.

entries.clue: Said to include one working in position (9)

indicatorNotes.to include: the word for said takes the other letters inside it

blocks.note: on = working, as in switched on

annotation.surface: Someone is reported to be including one employee in a job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Said' is not a sound signal here; it is simply a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A sentry or soldier assigned to a post is placed there, standing at the given spot.

entries.clue: A wry BBC joke turned out to be a bit of nonsense (11)

indicatorNotes.turned out: turned out as in turned inside out, so the letters come out in a new order

annotation.surface: A dry BBC comedy sketch proves to be silly stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is Lewis Carroll's famous nonsense poem from Through the Looking-Glass.
annotation.definitionFit: Carroll's poem is the classic piece of invented-word verse, and its title became a general word for meaningless talk.

entries.clue: Join a trade union (5)

blocks.note: one of Britain's largest unions, formed in 2007

annotation.surface: An invitation to sign up to a union.
annotation.walkthrough: The union is a big British one, created by a merger, whose name is itself the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To join forces is to combine, and the British union took that verb as its name.

entries.clue: City of Northern Aragon’s premier painter? (6)

indicatorNotes.premier: premier means first in rank, so take the first letter of Aragon

blocks.note: Francisco Goya, the Spanish painter, born in Aragon

annotation.surface: Asks which town is home to the leading painter of northern Aragon.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points to Spain, and Goya really was Aragonese, but the city is in Japan.
annotation.definitionFit: Nagoya is a major Japanese industrial port on Honshu, home to Toyota's region.

entries.clue: Iceberg rolls, killing one Cape diver (5)

indicatorNotes.rolls: an iceberg that rolls over ends up upside down, so the word is written backwards
indicatorNotes.killing: killing one and Cape means knocking those letters out

blocks.note: used as it stands, then reversed

annotation.surface: An iceberg capsizes and kills a diver off the Cape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diver' looks like a person in the sea off the Cape of Good Hope; it is a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Grebes are waterbirds that hunt fish by plunging underwater, so they are divers.

entries.clue: Vivid chart recalled Channel Islands (7)

indicatorNotes.recalled: re-called, called back, so the letters come back in reverse

annotation.surface: A colourful map of the Channel Islands is brought back to mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British islands off France: Jersey, Guernsey and others.
annotation.definitionFit: A description full of clear, lifelike detail, sometimes shockingly so, is called graphic.

entries.clue: Wandering in pursuit of black bird (9)

indicatorNotes.in pursuit of: a pursuer comes behind, so the wandering word follows black

annotation.surface: Someone roams around chasing a blackbird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black bird' looks like blackbird; 'black' gives one letter and 'bird' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The brambling is a finch related to the chaffinch, a winter visitor to Britain.

entries.clue: Cheap accommodation ultimately dodgy; the loo shut off (5,6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter
indicatorNotes.off: off as in gone off, spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A budget lodging turns out shabby, with its toilet out of use.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shut off' looks like a phrase about the toilet; 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: These budget lodgings offer dormitory beds to travellers, originally young walkers.

entries.clue: Bar nicely renovated hosting European male hip hop act (6,5)

indicatorNotes.renovated: a renovated thing is rebuilt, so nicely is rebuilt in a new order
indicatorNotes.hosting: a host takes guests in, so the rearranged letters take E and M inside

annotation.surface: A smartly refurbished bar puts on a European rapper.
annotation.walkthrough: The act is the American rap group behind 'Fight the Power'; the renovated bar is a real-looking venue for it.
annotation.definitionFit: The New York group led by Chuck D is one of the best-known rap outfits.

entries.clue: Republican lodged in a bogus religious retreat (6)

indicatorNotes.lodged in: a lodger lives inside someone else's house, so R goes inside

annotation.surface: A politician is hiding out in a fake place of worship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bogus' is an adjective in the surface but has to be read as a noun meaning a fake, with A in front.
annotation.definitionFit: A Hindu hermitage where people withdraw for meditation and study is called an ashram.

entries.clue: Helen’s lover to box out of bounds nobleman (10)

indicatorNotes.out of bounds: the bounds are the outer edges, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: Paris eloped with Helen of Troy

annotation.surface: Helen's lover is told to fight a nobleman out of bounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' applies to the whole string: the joined words lose only the P at the front and the E at the back.
annotation.definitionFit: A member of the hereditary titled class, such as a duke or earl, is an aristocrat.

entries.clue: Subjects against abandoning senses of rights and wrongs? (8)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: to abandon is to leave behind, so the word for against is left out

blocks.note: con = against, as in pros and cons; removed
your conscience tells right from wrong

annotation.surface: People give up their moral sense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Subjects' looks like people under a monarch; it means fields of study.
annotation.definitionFit: Physics, chemistry and biology are subjects taught at school, grouped as the sciences.

entries.clue: Quiet whiskies reportedly bringing on sentimentality (8)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: a report is something heard, so the letters come from a sound

annotation.surface: A few drinks make someone go all misty-eyed.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is Yiddish, literally 'chicken fat', which is why its spelling is so far from the sound.
annotation.definitionFit: The Yiddish word for rendered fat came to mean excessively sugary, tear-jerking style in music or film.

entries.clue: Senior churchman once a reformed character (3,3)

blocks.note: a 19th-century English cardinal, John Henry, canonised in 2019
someone who has changed his ways feels like a different person

annotation.surface: A senior cleric who has turned over a new leaf.
annotation.walkthrough: Cardinal Newman was himself a convert from Anglicanism, which gives 'reformed' an extra edge.
annotation.definitionFit: The cardinal's surname, split in two, describes a person transformed by turning over a new leaf.

entries.clue: Old king wildly threatened with large axe briefly (9,3,5)

indicatorNotes.wildly: things thrown about wildly land in any order, so the letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, cut short, so the axe loses its last letter

annotation.surface: An ancient ruler is menaced with a huge axe.
annotation.walkthrough: The American spelling 'ax' is not needed; the axe is just docked of its E before the letters are mixed.
annotation.definitionFit: The Macedonian ruler who conquered Persia in the fourth century BC was a king of ancient times.

entries.clue: Coarse abuse upset labour clergyman (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: upset means knocked over, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

annotation.surface: A Labour vicar is hurt by crude insults.
annotation.walkthrough: As a noun the answer is British slang for insults, as in 'giving someone some verbal'.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang uses the adjective as a noun for spoken insults, the kind shouted in a slanging match.

entries.clue: Sharp alpha male, whimsical Australian mostly on the inside (10)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.on the inside: the shortened word goes inside the alpha male

blocks.note: Alpha is A in the NATO alphabet
Strine is a jokey name for Australian English; drop the final E

annotation.surface: A sharp-tongued macho Australian who is somewhat eccentric underneath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strine' is Australian English spelt as an Australian says it, a humorous coinage, which is why it is whimsical. 'Alpha male' looks like one phrase but splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: An astringent remark stings like the lotion that tightens skin, so it is biting or severe.

entries.clue: Brilliant Independent covering church feature (8)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes round the outside, so the abbreviation wraps the church feature

blocks.note: a spire tops a church tower

annotation.surface: The Independent newspaper runs a superb piece on a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Independent covering' reads as a newspaper reporting on a story; the covering is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: An idea that seems to come from genius or divine prompting is called inspired, meaning outstanding.

entries.clue: Somehow thinks wife cheated, invoking puzzled query (4,3,7)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are put in some other way

annotation.surface: A husband suspects his wife has been unfaithful and asks what is going on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The dickens' is an old euphemism for the devil, nothing to do with the novelist.
annotation.definitionFit: The exclamation means 'what on earth?', a bewildered question with the devil politely renamed.

entries.clue: Considers sounding out routes to the summit (6,2)

indicatorNotes.sounding out: sounding out loud gives the sound of the phrase, not its spelling

annotation.surface: A climber studies the routes up a peak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sounding out' looks like part of the definition, as in sounding someone out; here it is the sound signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Assessing options as if balancing them on scales is to consider them carefully.

entries.clue: Some Rt Hon gentleman getting minimal coverage down under (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: some means a part of, so the answer is part of the next words

annotation.surface: An MP is caught wearing very little.
annotation.walkthrough: Rt Hon is the title of a senior British politician. 'Down under' plays on Australia, where the word means a flip-flop, and on the body's rear.
annotation.definitionFit: Skimpy underwear or swimwear that leaves the buttocks almost bare gives very little cover to one's behind.

entries.clue: Empty beer jug for tea maker (6)

indicatorNotes.Empty: an empty word has had its inside poured out, leaving only its outer letters

annotation.surface: A drinker swaps an empty beer jug for tea.
annotation.walkthrough: The beer in the surface nudges towards the obvious kind of brewer; here it is whoever makes the pot of tea.
annotation.definitionFit: Tea is brewed in a pot, so whoever makes it is doing the brewing.

entries.clue: Book of verse, indeed, just opened by idiot (6,4)

indicatorNotes.opened by: the idiot opens up the word for indeed and stands inside it

annotation.surface: An idiot opens a book of poems.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book of verse' looks like the definition; 'Book' alone is the definition and 'verse' is a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Thackeray's 1848 satirical novel about Becky Sharp is a book, named after a fair in Pilgrim's Progress.

entries.clue: In my opinion, low-down character of Shakespeare’s work (6)

annotation.surface: Someone gives their view of a lowly Shakespeare character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gen' is British slang for information.
annotation.definitionFit: Imogen is the heroine of Cymbeline, a late romance by the playwright.

entries.clue: African on CBS rubbished English philosopher (7,5)

indicatorNotes.rubbished: something rubbished is trashed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

annotation.surface: An African on an American TV network runs down a British thinker.
annotation.walkthrough: CBS is an American television network.
annotation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan statesman and essayist who championed the scientific method was an English philosopher.

entries.clue: Cover tip of finger in fresh guacamole (10)

indicatorNotes.tip of: the tip is the very end, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.in: in means placed inside, so the letter goes inside the rearranged dip
indicatorNotes.fresh: fresh means newly made, so the guacamole is remade in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone dips a fingertip into a newly made bowl of guacamole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a verb to go with the fingertip; it is a noun, the kind soldiers hide behind.
annotation.definitionFit: Disguise that hides soldiers or animals by blending into surroundings serves as cover.

entries.clue: Wasteful convent initially failing to collect tax by first of April (11)

indicatorNotes.initially failing: the part that comes initially fails, so the first letter drops away
indicatorNotes.to collect: the shortened convent collects the tax, taking it inside
indicatorNotes.first of: the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: cess is an old word for a local tax

annotation.surface: A convent falls behind on its tax bill by the start of April.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Convent' must first become a synonym before it loses its opening N.
annotation.definitionFit: Spending that serves no need is needless, so wasteful and unnecessary overlap.

entries.clue: Cave reached when crossing river (6)

indicatorNotes.crossing: a river crossing a road cuts through it, so R cuts into the other letters

annotation.surface: Travellers find a cave as they ford a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reached' must become a two-word phrase, run together.
annotation.definitionFit: A small picturesque cavern, natural or man-made, is a grotto.

entries.clue: I must visit doctor, working somewhere in the field (3-2)

indicatorNotes.must visit: a visitor goes inside, so I goes into the doctor

annotation.surface: A farmhand needs to see a doctor while out working the fields.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a cricket fielding position, in front of the batsman on the leg side; 'field' is the cricket field, not a farm.
annotation.definitionFit: Cricket names the places where fielders stand, and this one lies straight-ish in front on the leg side.

entries.clue: Met Estonian’s renovated split-level home (11)

indicatorNotes.renovated: a renovated building is rebuilt, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters; the 's reads as 'is'

annotation.surface: Someone meets an Estonian whose flat has been done up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Estonian's' is read as 'Estonian is', joining the fodder to its indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A flat spread over two floors of a building, with its own entrance, is a split-level home.

entries.clue: Penny and Heather admitting Daisy is laying it on a bit thick, perhaps (10)

annotation.definition: laying it on a bit thick, perhaps

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit is to let in, so heather lets the daisy inside

blocks.note: ling is a kind of heather
the aster is a daisy-like flower

annotation.surface: Penny and Heather tell Daisy she is overdoing it.
annotation.walkthrough: Penny, Heather and Daisy look like three women's names; they are a coin and two plants.
annotation.definitionFit: Spreading wet plaster over a wall means applying it thickly; 'perhaps' flags this as one example of laying something on.

entries.clue: Strangle Will in chaotic hand-to-hand combat (3-2,9)

indicatorNotes.chaotic: chaotic means without order, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: Someone chokes a man called Will during a free-for-all brawl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' belongs to the fodder even though it reads as a link to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Freestyle wrestling with few holds barred is a sport of grappling bare-handed with an opponent.

entries.clue: Cut sauce which has been thickened (9)

blocks.note: a noun: a lowering, as in a price cut
a cooking term for liquid boiled down to concentrate it

annotation.surface: A chef trims down a thickened sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: In cooking, a sauce simmered until much of its water evaporates is named after the shrinking.
annotation.definitionFit: Lowering a price and boiling down a sauce both make something smaller, hence the one word for both.

entries.clue: Blood sport, day one: endless avarice (8)

indicatorNotes.endless: endless means without an end, so the word for avarice loses its last letter

annotation.surface: On the first day of a hunt, greed takes over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blood sport' reads as one phrase, like fox hunting; 'Blood' alone is the definition, meaning lineage.
annotation.definitionFit: Blood, as in 'of royal blood', means ancestry or breeding, a recorded line of descent.

entries.clue: Dismal signal from conductor (8)

blocks.note: the baton stroke that marks the first beat of a bar

annotation.surface: A gloomy gesture from an orchestra's conductor.
annotation.walkthrough: The conductor's gesture is a downward stroke of the baton, the first beat of each bar.
annotation.definitionFit: A gloomy mood and the baton's first stroke share the word, one figurative and one literal.

entries.clue: Walked daintily around ground (6)

blocks.note: moved about with small, affected steps
past tense of grind, as meat is through a grinder

annotation.surface: Someone tiptoed round a patch of land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun, the land walked around; it is the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb covers both prancing with prissy steps and chopping meat finely in a grinder.

entries.clue: Greek god sat for artist, covering one leg (8)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes over something, so the word for sat wraps round one

blocks.note: in cricket the leg side is also the on side

annotation.surface: A model sits for a painter as a Greek god, draped over one leg.
annotation.walkthrough: The leg side of a cricket field is also called the on side, which is where the last chunk comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Poseidon ruled the sea in Greek myth, the brother of Zeus.

entries.clue: Formal accessory page Henry wears fitting perfectly (3,3)

indicatorNotes.wears: clothing that is worn goes around the wearer, so the phrase goes around P and H

blocks.note: H = henry, the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: A page boy called Henry puts on a perfectly fitting hat.
annotation.walkthrough: The grammar runs backwards: 'page Henry wears' means the phrase for fitting perfectly is worn around the two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat worn with morning dress or tails completes formal attire.

entries.clue: Style of writing with a tendency to lean to the right? (6)

annotation.definition: Style of writing with a tendency to lean to the right?

blocks.note: sounds like a journalist's style, but means a kind of lettering

blocks.clueFragment: with a tendency to lean to the right?
blocks.note: sounds political, but means slanting physically rightwards

annotation.surface: A political writer with right-wing sympathies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lean to the right' suggests politics; it is literal, the slant of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes forward to the right, unlike upright roman type.

entries.clue: One likes to drag small donkey over river (6)

indicatorNotes.over: over means on top, and in a down clue the top comes first

blocks.note: moke is British slang for a donkey

annotation.surface: Someone enjoys hauling a little donkey across a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drag' looks like hauling; it is a puff on a cigarette.
annotation.definitionFit: A drag is a puff on a cigarette, so a person who enjoys them is a tobacco user.

entries.clue: Inspirational sister moved priest with task (11)

indicatorNotes.moved: letters that are moved change places, so priest is rearranged

annotation.surface: An inspiring nun's words stirred a priest at work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sister' looks like a nun; the nine Muses were sisters who inspired the arts.
annotation.definitionFit: Terpsichore is the Muse of dance, one of the nine daughters of Zeus who inspire artists.

entries.clue: Competitive driver, one in fancy car (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed inside, so the one sits inside the car

blocks.note: an ace counts as one in cards

annotation.surface: A racing driver sits in a posh car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an anagram signal for 'car'; it is a description of the luxury make.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who drives in races against other drivers competes on the track.

entries.clue: Last character used to symbolise the resistance? (5)

blocks.note: the final letter of the Greek alphabet
the symbol for ohms, the unit of electrical resistance

annotation.surface: The final figure in a story becomes the emblem of an underground movement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The resistance' looks like a wartime movement; it is electrical resistance, measured in ohms.
annotation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet ends with it, and physicists write it as the ohm's symbol.

entries.clue: Teller of tellers? (4,7)

blocks.note: read as one who tells, here one who gives orders

annotation.surface: A storyteller who tells stories about storytellers.
annotation.walkthrough: A teller is also a cashier, and the person who tells cashiers what to do runs the branch.
annotation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a branch directs its cashiers, telling the tellers.

entries.clue: Quick police operation featuring Robocop finally (5)

indicatorNotes.featuring: a show featuring someone has them in it, so the letter goes inside
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so take the last letter

annotation.surface: A swift police raid starring the film cyborg Robocop.
annotation.walkthrough: Robocop is the robot policeman of the 1987 film, which suits the police surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Movement happening at great speed, such as a pulse or river current, is described as fast.

entries.clue: Four opening large uniform chest producing a lot of money (9)

indicatorNotes.opening: four opens the chest up and sits inside it

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Four people prise open a big chest of uniforms and find a fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like an adjective describing the four; it is the verb, prising the chest apart.
annotation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin lucrum, profit, so a lucrative deal pays handsomely.

entries.clue: Under control, remove phosphorous and boron from copper zinc alloy (2,5)

indicatorNotes.remove: remove means take away, so the two named letters are taken out

blocks.note: phosphorus's chemical symbol taken as the letter, removed
B = boron, its chemical symbol; removed
pinchbeck is a copper-zinc alloy once used as fake gold

annotation.surface: A metallurgist purifies brass by removing phosphorus and boron.
annotation.walkthrough: The alloy is named after its inventor, the watchmaker Christopher Pinchbeck. The chemistry surface makes the two elements look like real impurities.
annotation.definitionFit: Held back or restrained, like a chess king threatened into limited moves, means being kept under control.

entries.clue: Idiot stealing article from continental port (5)

indicatorNotes.stealing: stealing takes something away, so the article is removed
indicatorNotes.from: from marks where the article is taken out of, the port's name

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article; removed

annotation.surface: A fool is caught stealing goods from a European harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Continental' is the British way of saying mainland European.
annotation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, a mild British insult.

entries.clue: Continue film franchise (5,2)

blocks.note: a long-running series of British bawdy comedies, 1958 to 1992

annotation.surface: Keep a series of films going.
annotation.walkthrough: The films are British comedies full of double entendres, from Sergeant in 1958 onwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means keep going, and each film title in the series began with it.

entries.clue: Element of technical language judge dismissed (5)

indicatorNotes.dismissed: a judge who is dismissed is sent out, so the letter J leaves the word

annotation.surface: A legal term is thrown out when the judge dismisses the case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Element' looks like a component of the language; it is a chemical element.
annotation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, number 18 on the periodic table.

entries.clue: Deeply troubled auditor men tediously cut down to size (9)

indicatorNotes.cut down to size: trimmed at both ends, so only the middle stretch of the words remains

annotation.surface: Auditors are dull men who get belittled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut down to size' usually means humbled; here it trims the three words at both ends.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone suffering great anguish or mental pain is described as tormented.
